entries.title: Who is Andy Burnham, the U.K.'s new prime minister?
entries.snippet: On Monday, former Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham succeeds Keir Starmer as the United Kingdom's prime minister. Burnham's politics have been shaped by England's north-south class divide.

entries.title: Violence repeatedly erupts in dementia care despite warnings, inspections show

entries.title: 5 clever design tricks to make a small home look bigger

entries.title: Cuban artist and dissident exiled from country after 5 years in prison arrives in US

entries.title: MLS works to bring in a new generation of fans as the World Cup comes to an end

entries.title: Spain is the 2026 World Cup champion, defeating Argentina for its 2nd title
entries.snippet: Spain's run to the title was a defensive masterclass, with wins over four of the world's top ten teams. They are the first World Cup champion to win the title while only conceding a single goal.

entries.snippet: The Republican vice president's growing family is in keeping with his passionate advocacy for Americans to have more children.

entries.title: PHOTOS: Spain wins the World Cup by beating Argentina 1-0 on Ferran Torres' goal in extra time
entries.snippet: Denying Lionel Messi a second straight title in what he has indicated would be his final World Cup match, Torres came off the bench and scored in the 106th minute and Spain ended Argentina's reign with a 1-0 win on Sunday.

entries.title: Mount Olympus, home of the ancient Greek gods, vies for World Heritage status
entries.snippet: The nomination is to be discussed when the World Heritage Committee meets in Busan, South Korea, from Sunday through July 29.

entries.title: Nigerian children pay the price for the Iran war as malnutrition and poverty surge

entries.snippet: The outbreak on Manhattan's Upper East Side has infected 72 people, according to health officials.

entries.title: Goals, technology and hydration breaks: How the biggest World Cup in history will be remembered

entries.title: Darline Graham's career centered disability. Now she could help shape national policy
entries.snippet: To former colleagues and the disability advocates who have worked with her, there is little doubt in Darline Graham's capabilities.

entries.title: David Crowley reenters battleground Wisconsin's Democratic governor primary with Gov. Evers' backing
entries.snippet: Gov. Tony Evers initially declined to endorse in the race but threw his weight behind Crowley and resuscitated his bid to lead the swing state known for razor-thin election margins.

entries.title: Texas Hill Country floods test new warning systems after last year's deadly disaster
entries.snippet: Residents in some hard-hit areas said a year of preparation did make a difference. Newly installed flood sirens sounded in the darkness. Phones buzzed with alerts that weren't sent out last year.

entries.snippet: Many of the attacks have been carried out by angry mobs who have stormed treatment centers or targeted response teams in the field, Pierre Akilimali, incident manager for the Ebola response, said at a press briefing.

entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Spain win World Cup for second time after beating Argentina 1-0
entries.snippet: After a 16 year wait, Spain have claimed a second men's World Cup. Ferran Torres scored the winner in a deserved 1-0 victory over Argentina, which means Spain are now men’s and women’s world champions.

entries.title: New Bundesliga TV deal in US prioritizes reach over money
entries.snippet: The Bundesliga has a new home on American screens after Germany's top football league left ESPN. The new deal is a sign of the times.

entries.title: Algeria seeks larger EU energy role amid regional tensions
entries.snippet: Algeria and Germany agreed to deepen energy ties during President Abdelmadjid Tebboune's recent visit to Berlin. But Algiers is still grappling with tensions at home, over Western Sahara and instability in the Sahel.

entries.title: Germany news: Merz moots Cabinet reshuffle after Spahn exit
entries.snippet: Chancellor Merz has said he might use the forced resignation of a senior ally as a chance to reshuffle his Cabinet. Meanwhile, a train security guard was critically injured in a clash with a passenger. DW has more.

entries.title: Spain: Emergency crews battle wildfire north of Madrid
entries.snippet: More than 25 firefighting planes have been deployed to battle the blaze in central Spain, which has been raging for three days.

entries.title: Fact check: Spotting AI-generated 'historical' images

entries.title: EU ban on destroying unsold clothes takes effect
entries.snippet: Under new rules to reduce waste, large companies across the European Union can no longer dispose of unsold clothes, accessories and footwear.

entries.title: China firm seeks damages over state control of British Steel
entries.snippet: The UK government took over British Steel last year to prevent the closure of the country's last primary steelmaking facility. China's Jingye Group, which bought the firm in 2020, claims it is owed compensation.

entries.title: Russian army deserters in Germany: 'No choice but to run'
entries.snippet: Almost all asylum applications by Russian deserters are being denied by German authorities. DW and Russian-language media outlet Astra spoke to one of the young men who fears he'll be sent back to die on the front lines.

entries.title: Israel clears way for crocodiles to stop prison breaks
entries.snippet: Israel's environment minister has reclassified crocodiles so that they can now be used for security purposes. Far-right Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir reportedly wants them to surround a jail holding Hamas militants.

entries.title: Russia's largest ballistic assault of war rocks Kyiv
entries.snippet: Fires broke out across the Ukrainian capital after Russia's latest missile attack, which used the highest number of ballistic missiles of the war so far. Several people have been injured in Kyiv.

entries.title: Andrew Tate, brother arrested in Miami, UK seeks extradition
entries.snippet: Andrew and Tristan Tate were taken into custody by the US Marshals Service in Miami on a sealed warrant. The UK has requested their extradition on charges that include trafficking and rape.

entries.title: France's Mbappe sets World Cup scoring record with 22 goals
entries.snippet: Kylian Mbappe has moved past Lionel Messi on the all-time World Cup goal-scoring record in a spectacular match for third place. England won the game 6-4.

entries.title: Cuban dissident artist arrives in US after 5 years in prison
entries.snippet: Luis Manuel Otero Alcantara, a prominent Cuban artist and dissident, was detained in July 2021 as he attempted to join unprecedented mass protests across the communist island.

entries.title: Hungary's president signs amendment ending his own term
entries.snippet: An ally of former PM Viktor Orban has signed a constitutional amendment ending his own term as head of state. Tamas Sulyok criticized the law, while lawmakers insist he has impeded national progress by staying in office.

entries.title: Germany: CDU's Jens Spahn resigns amid surrogacy controversy
entries.snippet: Surrogacy is not permitted in Germany and the conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) opposes its legalization. Spahn and his husband had their child through a surrogate mother in the US.

entries.title: Norway: Huge fire destroys 100 homes, sparks evacuations
entries.snippet: Firefighters from other areas of Norway were drafted in to help tackle the blaze in the southern city of Drammen.

entries.title: Segregation in Israel: Separate streets for men and women?
entries.snippet: An Israeli city with a large ultra-Orthodox Jewish population wants to segregate men and women on certain streets. Israeli politicians have voted to allow university courses to do the same.

entries.title: US strikes Iran after 2 service members killed in Jordan
entries.snippet: The US military struck Iran after two US soldiers were reported killed in an Iranian attack on a US base in Jordan. Meanwhile, Kuwait and Bahrain reported fresh Iranian attacks.
